note: Prosody is taught, not drilled: the skill's only kind is `recognise`, and there is nothing to parse or fill in. So this file holds four illustrative lines of our own verse rather than the twelve practice sentences a drillable skill gets, and each carries its scansion in `scan`. Every word is inside the cumulative vocabulary to chapter 34 or a name of the book's cast; because the lines are ours and not the poets', a learner may be shown a whole line marked long and short without quoting anyone.

sentences.la: Laetae nunc caelum spectant sub lūce puellae.
sentences.en: Happy girls are looking at the sky now in the light.
sentences.scan: Lae tae | nunc cae | lum spec | tant sub | lū ce pu | el lae  —  – – | – – | – – | – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | – –
sentences.note: An illustrative hexameter of our own, not a practice sentence. Both syllables of Laetae are long because both hold a diphthong: ae. So are cae- in caelum and -lae in puellae; lū- is long because its vowel is long.

sentences.la: Ipse pater noster nostrum servābat amīcum.
sentences.en: Our own father was watching over our friend.
sentences.scan: Ip se pa | ter nos | ter nos | trum ser | vā ba ta | mī cum  —  – ⏑ ⏑ | – – | – – | – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | – –
sentences.note: An illustrative hexameter of our own, not a practice sentence. The o of noster is a short vowel, yet nos- is a long syllable, because s and t follow it. So are Ip-, -ter, -trum and ser-.

sentences.la: Iūlia et Aemilia stant nunc in lītore sōlae.
sentences.en: Julia and Aemilia are standing alone on the shore now.
sentences.scan: Iūli(a) et | Aemili | a stant | nunc in | lī to re | sō lae  —  – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – – | – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | – –
sentences.note: An illustrative hexameter of our own, not a practice sentence. The final -a of Iūlia is swallowed before the e of et, so the line has fifteen syllables to read, not the sixteen it prints.

sentences.la: Nunc taceō, quia nōn habeō quod dīcere possum.
sentences.en: Now I say nothing, because I have nothing I can say.
sentences.scan: Nunc ta ce | ō qui a | nōn ha be | ō quod | dī ce re | pos sum  —  – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | – –
sentences.note: An illustrative hexameter of our own, not a practice sentence. Every rule at once: -ō is long by its own vowel, pos- is long because two consonants follow it, and qui- and -a are both short.
